purpose: Colesevelam is used to lower bad cholesterol (LDL) in your blood to help protect your heart. It is also used to help control blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes when used along with other diabetes medicines. Lowering your cholesterol reduces your risk of heart attack and stroke.
how_it_works: Your body makes bile acids in your liver using cholesterol. Colesevelam works like a sponge in your gut — it grabs onto bile acids and carries them out of your body in your stool instead of letting them be reabsorbed. Because your liver then needs to use more cholesterol to make new bile acids, the cholesterol level in your blood goes down.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are stomach-related, such as constipation, upset stomach, nausea, gas, and bloating. Drinking plenty of water and eating enough fiber can help ease these symptoms.
warnings: This medicine can interfere with how your body absorbs other medicines and vitamins, so take your other medications at least 4 hours before or after colesevelam. It should not be used if you have a history of bowel blockage, very high triglycerides, or inflammation of the pancreas (pancreatitis). Tell your doctor about all medications and supplements you take. It is not recommended during pregnancy.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is either three 625 mg tablets taken twice a day with meals, or six tablets once a day with a meal. It also comes as a powder packet mixed with water. Always take it with food and a full glass of liquid.
